status_summary: Force Design continues under the Commandant's 2025 Force Design Update, released 2025-10-23. The Marine Corps force design page states that 3d Marine Littoral Regiment reached initial operating capability in December 2023, 12th Marine Littoral Regiment is projected to reach it in 2026, and 4th Marine Regiment is retained as a reinforced infantry regiment rather than converted into a third littoral regiment (Military Times reports the same). For the light amphibious ship, P.L. 119-21 provides 160 million dollars in advance procurement and about 1.8 billion dollars for Landing Ship Medium procurement per CRS, Sec. 127 of the FY2026 NDAA (P.L. 119-60, 2025-12-18) authorizes contracts for not more than 15 Medium Landing Ships after a 30-day advance certification to Congress, and CRS reports the Navy selected the LST-100 design in December 2025, with construction expected from late 2026 and first delivery wanted by 2029. Federal law (10 U.S.C. 8062(b), added in 2022) already requires not less than 31 operational amphibious warfare ships, 10 of them assault ships; the 381-ship plan described by CRS includes 18 LSMs against a Marine Corps goal of 35. The update describes a rifle squad led by a school-trained sergeant, and no source was found on E-6 squad leaders, specific divestments or the current count of amphibious ships.

timeline.event: Reconciliation law P.L. 119-21 enacted; per CRS its Sec. 20002 provides 160 million dollars in advance procurement and about 1.8 billion dollars for Landing Ship Medium procurement.

Commandant issues the 2025 Force Design Update; the Marine Corps force design page states that 3d Marine Littoral Regiment reached initial operating capability in December 2023, that 12th Marine Littoral Regiment is projected to reach it in 2026, and that 4th Marine Regiment is retained as a reinforced infantry regiment, with two littoral regiments and one reinforced regiment described as the best composition for III MEF. The page also describes a return to a 13-Marine rifle squad with three fire teams led by a school-trained sergeant, a three-phase Medium Landing Ship program, and the statutory floor of 31 operational amphibious ships.

(month-only date) The Navy announced that it selected the Damen LST-100 design for the initial Medium Landing Ships, with construction expected from late 2026 and first delivery wanted by 2029, per CRS report R46374 (updated 2026-01-13).

FY2026 NDAA signed as P.L. 119-60. Sec. 127 authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to contract for not more than 15 Medium Landing Ships, including additions to existing contracts, after certifying to the congressional defense committees at least 30 days beforehand on force structure consistency, savings, funding, design stability and cost estimates. Per U.S. Code notes, the Act did not change the 31-ship floor in 10 U.S.C. 8062(b) but added a paragraph on prioritizing maintenance to keep the minimum number of amphibious warfare ships available.
